programme: MNT and CIC are two independent transcriptional brakes on the two classic proliferation-driving oncogenic axes: MNT is a MAX-interacting bHLHZ repressor that antagonizes MYC:MAX at shared targets, and its recovered target set here includes MAX itself plus TERT, CCND2, KRAS and TP53 — the canonical MYC/MAX cell-cycle and telomerase readout. CIC is the RAS-MAPK-repressed HMG-box repressor whose recovered targets (ETV5, RASA1, CCNE1) are its textbook substrates (PEA3-family ETV genes, a RAS-GAP, and cyclin E1). Together they read as the transcriptional restraint on MYC- and RAS-driven cell-cycle entry (TERT/CCND2/CCNE1/KRAS), not a physical complex but a matched pair of growth checkpoints.
role_in_a: If this restraint is lost, de-repression of TERT, CCND2, CCNE1 and KRAS would drive vascular smooth muscle cell cycle re-entry, the proliferative step underlying neointimal hyperplasia, plaque growth and restenosis — a generic but real vascular-injury proliferation signature.
role_in_b: The same restraint, if lost, is the documented route to unchecked proliferation in other tissues (CIC loss drives CIC-DUX4 sarcoma and oligodendroglioma; MYC/MAX-network reactivation of TERT is a generic immortalization step), and would be expected to play an analogous role restraining neoplastic thymic epithelial proliferation.
shared_axis: Both diseases involve pathological proliferation of a resident, normally quiescent tissue cell (vascular smooth muscle vs. thymic epithelium), and could converge on the same MYC/RAS cell-cycle checkpoint machinery, with MNT and CIC recurring as its transcriptional brakes in both tissues' inferred networks.
reasoning: The module itself is nameable and internally consistent — MNT's targets are the textbook MYC/MAX/TERT signature and CIC's are its textbook RAS-MAPK substrates — but nothing in the retrieved record places either factor in cardiovascular disease, Open Targets scores for both in thymoma are low-to-mid percentile at best, and ReMap shows zero observed MNT binding at any of its own ten targets. No documented link between thymoma and cardiovascular disease runs through this axis, and the tissues are not obviously paired by anatomy or clinical practice, so the account stands on the coherence of the module alone rather than on anything retrieved.
support: none found — no retrieved paper for MNT or CIC was judged on-topic for either disease (reader's notes mark all as off-topic or ambiguous). NCOA4's PMID 42420246 places NCOA4 in thymic epithelial tumors, but NCOA4 is not part of this growth-control module and its targets (AR, KLK3, TFF1) belong to a separate androgen-receptor thread.
how_to_falsify: Knock down MNT and CIC separately in a vascular-injury/restenosis model (e.g. balloon-injured rat carotid or human VSMCs in culture) and in a thymic epithelial tumor cell line, then assay TERT, CCND2, CCNE1 and KRAS expression and proliferation in both. If loss of either factor fails to de-repress these shared targets and fails to increase proliferation in both cell types, the shared-checkpoint account is false; ChIP/CUT&RUN confirming MNT does not occupy the MAX/TERT/CCND2 loci in VSMCs (consistent with the 0/10 ReMap result already seen) would further undercut it.
caveats: Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 80 patient-group comparisons, so the denominator overstates independence. 'Cardiovascular_Disease' here is an undifferentiated label with no Open Targets association for either factor, so the vascular-proliferation framing (atherosclerosis/restenosis) is an assumption about cohort composition, not a given fact. The exclusion lists rule out two easy alternative explanations: this is not a single-subgroup artifact (CUX1, FOXP2, IRF5 and others that led one group did not recur elsewhere), and it is not just re-detecting generic blood/thymus regulators (STAT5A/B, AR, IRF8, MEF2C, NFATC1, CEBPD were already removed as tissue-generic).
